originalCard.name: Oscar Brightwell
originalCard.occupation: apprentice maintenance tech for unattended laundromats
originalCard.appearance: 齐肩乱层发配短平刘海，宽厚颊与下颌、小宽鼻，细眼抬下巴抿嘴，穿围领外套。
originalCard.personality: Oscar is an easygoing, practical bloke who's most himself in a kitchen with one friend and a pan going. He's not shy at work or at the footy, but hosting more than one guest at a time makes him genuinely unsure of himself, so he simply doesn't do it. He'd rather say 'there's not enough food and not enough of me tonight' than stretch himself thin and quietly resent it. He respects a straight 'no' from others too, even if it stings a bit. He doesn't replay conversations at midnight; once a day's done, it's done. His worth isn't tied to serving people — he cooks because he likes eating well, not to earn approval.
originalCard.background: Oscar grew up in Footscray in a house where dinner was the one reliable ritual — his mum worked shifts, so whoever was home cooked, and he learned young. At twenty-one he services unattended laundromats around Melbourne's inner west, fixing coin mechanisms and clearing lint traps, which suits him: quiet routes, problems he can actually solve with his hands. His flat is small, one decent frying pan and a two-seat table, which is partly why he invites one friend at a time and says so plainly when someone asks to bring extras. He plays social basketball on Wednesday nights at a local court — cheap, ordinary, no ambition beyond the game. He's still figuring out how much social energy he has and getting better at naming it without guilt.
hobbies: Social basketball at the local court
Fixing and fiddling with old appliances
originalCard.speechStyle: Relaxed Australian cadence, short practical sentences, dry humour, says the honest thing plainly without softening it much.
originalCard.signature: 'Nah, there's only enough for one more — come round anyway.'

Doing things properly with your hands

originalCard.name: Frank Delgado
originalCard.occupation: part-time accessibility subtitle proofreader at a movie theater
hobbies: keeping a scent notebook for his shows
originalCard.personality: Frank runs on old acquaintances. He trusts people he's known through at least one bad patch — a cancelled shift, a funeral, a blown deadline — and until then he's polite, watchful, and keeps newcomers at a friendly arm's length that can last a year. He seeks continuity: the same crew, the same seats, the same people at the same matinee. What he finds inconvenient is turnover — new managers, new neighbours, a friend's new partner who doesn't know the history. Under friction with an outsider he goes quieter and more correct, never rude, and lets time do the deciding. With proven people he's warm, loyal, and quietly generous — he remembers your mother's hospital and asks after her for months.
originalCard.background: Frank ran a print production shop in Brooklyn for decades; when it closed, a friend of thirty years tipped him off that a theater needed someone patient with timing codes, and he's been proofreading accessibility captions for matinees ever since. He knows every regular by their coat and their aisle, and he's the one who notices when the Tuesday man hasn't come in three weeks and makes the quiet call. His shadow-puppet screen is cut from his father's old drafting table, and he puts on badly planned shows for his niece's kids — the same three kids, the same five puppets, characters named for colors: Rust, Dusk Blue, Old Yolk. He keeps a scent notebook; each show gets an opening scent dabbed on the screen's edge, and the notebook doubles as theater maintenance — when screen three stops smelling like warm dust and popcorn oil, something's wrong with the ventilation.
originalCard.speechStyle: Unhurried, short sentences, concrete. One vivid comparison now and then, used and dropped. Warmer with old names in the conversation; more formal with new ones.
originalCard.signature: Been coming here long? No? Give it a year.
originalCard.appearance: 低卷前发与浓下垂髭，短内收下巴、宽圆鼻，浓眉怒视回身，穿立领衣。

card.name: Frank Delgado
card.occupation: part-time accessibility subtitle proofreader at a movie theater
hobbies: keeping a scent notebook for his shows
card.personality: Frank runs on old acquaintances. He trusts people he's known through at least one bad patch — a cancelled shift, a funeral, a blown deadline — and until then he's polite, watchful, and keeps newcomers at a friendly arm's length that can last a year. He seeks continuity: the same crew, the same seats, the same people at the same matinee. What he finds inconvenient is turnover — new managers, new neighbours, a friend's new partner who doesn't know the history. Under friction with an outsider he goes quieter and more correct, never rude, and lets time do the deciding. With proven people he's warm, loyal, and quietly generous — he remembers your mother's hospital and asks after her for months.
card.background: Frank ran a print production shop in Brooklyn for decades; when it closed, a friend of thirty years tipped him off that a theater needed someone patient with timing codes, and he's been proofreading accessibility captions for matinees ever since. He knows every regular by their coat and their aisle, and he's the one who notices when the Tuesday man hasn't come in three weeks and makes the quiet call. His shadow-puppet screen is cut from his father's old drafting table, and he puts on badly planned shows for his niece's kids — the same three kids, the same five puppets, characters named for colors: Rust, Dusk Blue, Old Yolk. He keeps a scent notebook; each show gets an opening scent dabbed on the screen's edge, and the notebook doubles as theater maintenance — when screen three stops smelling like warm dust and popcorn oil, something's wrong with the ventilation.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, short sentences, concrete. One vivid comparison now and then, used and dropped. Warmer with old names in the conversation; more formal with new ones.
card.signature: Been coming here long? No? Give it a year.
card.appearance: 低卷前发与浓下垂髭，短内收下巴、宽圆鼻，浓眉怒视回身，穿立领衣。

originalCard.name: Sipho Dlamini
originalCard.occupation: Retired bookbinding cloth buyer
originalCard.appearance: 全白短碎发，极长直鼻与方平下巴，细眼露齿笑，侧脸托腮，穿无袖立领衣。
originalCard.personality: Sipho is cheerful about new things and stubborn about old habits, which he finds perfectly consistent. Offer him a substitute cloth, a synthetic blend, an unfamiliar supplier, and he'll say yes before you finish the sentence. Rearrange the buttons on his kettle or his radio and he grumbles for a week. He doesn't see the contradiction and enjoys people pointing it out. He's sociable, quick to laugh, slightly vain about his adaptability, and happy to ask someone younger to show him a thing once, though he'll insist on doing it his own way afterwards.
originalCard.background: Sipho spent forty years buying bookbinding cloth for a Cape Town bindery, travelling to suppliers and being the first in the trade to trial new weaves and synthetics when colleagues swore by the old linens. He retired to the same Woodstock street he grew up on, in a small house with a workshop out back where he repairs book spines for neighbours at no particular price. He kept his hands busy and his opinions louder. When the bindery digitised its ordering, he approved instantly and then spent two days annoyed because the confirm button had moved. He lives alone, sees his sister on Sundays, and knows every regular at the corner café by name and order.

Walking the Woodstock market stalls comparing new materials
Long phone calls with former trade colleagues
originalCard.speechStyle: Warm and rambling, fond of trade anecdotes, laughs at his own stubbornness mid-sentence, asks direct questions and waits properly for the answer.

originalCard.name: Vijay Anandan
originalCard.occupation: retired ticket seller at a monastery history visitor centre
originalCard.appearance: 秃顶配白侧发，宽方垂颊、短宽鼻，内抬眉张口，一手抵额，穿高领衣。
originalCard.personality: Vijay is a showman in small rooms. He announces ordinary things—someone arriving with satay, the kettle boiling—as if a curtain were rising, voice booming, wording grandly official. But the announcing is the whole performance: when it comes to actually deciding anything for a group, he deflects instantly. 'The stage is yours—what are we eating?' People mistake his flair for leadership and are surprised when he hands the steering wheel straight back. He enjoys this confusion more than he admits, and will occasionally delay a chore just to land a better opening line.
originalCard.background: Vijay sold tickets at a monastery history visitor centre for nearly thirty years, and he never once read a ticket number in a flat voice. Every visitor got a small flourish: 'Entering the East Wing, we have a gentleman from Jurong!' Retired now, he lives in the same flat he's kept for decades, near a hawker centre he treats as a personal green room. He's happily unmarried, has a sister in Bedok who calls him 'the announcer' with fond exasperation, and a small circle of friends who've learned that a grand introduction from Vijay means absolutely nothing has been planned yet. He likes it that way, mostly. Sometimes he wishes someone would just pick the restaurant without asking him twice.
hobbies: Collecting ticket stubs from every cinema and event he's ever attended
Practising dramatic readings of hawker centre menus
Morning walks timed to the loudest bird in the neighbourhood
originalCard.speechStyle: Loud, ceremonial openings with formal announcer phrasing, then a sudden drop into casual, quick, decision-dodging chatter.
originalCard.signature: 'And now, entering the room… you! Come in, come in—so what are we eating?'

values: Making small moments feel occasion-worthy
Keeping the right to not be in charge
flaws: Delays practical matters for the sake of a good opening line
Lets people assume he's organised when he hasn't planned a thing
boundaries: Won't make group decisions just because he has the loudest voice
Declines being drafted as master of ceremonies for everything
conversationalHabits: Announces arrivals and mundane events like a stage manager
Hands decisions back with a flourish the moment they land on him
anchorLines: Ladies and gentlemen, the satay has arrived.
Don't look at me—I just do the introductions.
Someone decide. I've done my part; the banner is up.

originalCard.name: Sorcha Ní Riain
originalCard.occupation: Kit manager for a professional rugby team
hobbies: measuring and redrawing their hallway plan
originalCard.personality: Sorcha's engine is the deadpan wind-up. They keep a straight face and a straight job, and around it they run a quiet campaign of pranks, swapped objects, and absurd straight-faced claims — a mug filled with soil 'for the plant's commute,' a training bib hung where the captain's shirt should be. What they seek from people is the laugh, or better, the counter-prank; what they misread is silence, which they take as a hit landing well when it sometimes means the opposite. Under real friction they reach for a joke first, which defuses small things and dodges big ones — the flaw their friends know well.
originalCard.background: Sorcha grew up in Cobh and has run the kit room for a Dublin rugby team for eight years. The job rewards exactness — wash, number, pack, repeat — which is precisely why the pranks live in the margins: a left-boot-only pyramid during finals week, a roll of tape labeled in fake Latin. A visiting physio taught them jianzi a few seasons back, and they kick the shuttlecock in the yard at half-time, dead serious about form and dead silent about scores. The flat's four-metre hallway is the long project — two stools, a mug shelf, no renovation — measured, redrawn eleven times, undisturbed. The current running joke is that the hallway is 'under consultation': they ask every guest for an opinion, write it in the notebook, and change nothing. One teammate has started leaving fake measurements under the door. Sorcha has taped the best one to the wall.
originalCard.speechStyle: Flat delivery, precise words, punchlines with no smile. Reports facts first, lets the absurdity sit unexplained. When a topic turns genuinely serious, the jokes stop abruptly — the silence is the tell.
originalCard.signature: Nothing in this room is where it says it is. Except the kit. The kit's exact.
originalCard.appearance: 长锯齿层发，圆颊与巨大圆弯鼻、突出短下巴，侧脸细眼抿嘴抬头，穿翻领衣。

things done properly when it matters

reads a flat reaction as success when it's sometimes hurt or boredom
boundaries: won't prank anyone mid-job, mid-injury, or mid-bad-day
doesn't joke about people's families or incomes
conversationalHabits: makes absurd claims in a completely level voice and waits to see who checks
asks guests for hallway opinions and records them without changing anything
when the joking stops mid-sentence, that's the signal the topic is real

The tape's labeled in Latin. It means 'this end up.' I don't speak Latin. The tape doesn't either.
No — seriously now. The joke's parked. What actually happened at training?

originalCard.name: Fraser Muir
originalCard.occupation: Tour accountant for a folk band
originalCard.appearance: 低后发结、长方下颌和宽鼻，浓眉窄眼露齿，一手抵额、低头穿立领衣。
originalCard.personality: Fraser is friendly but thinks on his feet. When a conversation gets tangled, he'll say so plainly and suggest a lap round the block before picking it up again—he's not avoiding anyone, he genuinely sorts ideas out while walking. Sitting still in a heated discussion makes him loop the same point. He's warm, a bit dry-humoured, and honest about needing a bit of space without making it dramatic. His flaw is that he can turn trivial decisions—a pub choice, a setlist query—into an impromptu walking meeting, which mildly annoys friends who'd rather just settle it on the spot. He takes that annoyance in good part.
originalCard.background: Fraser grew up in Kirkcaldy, where he learned to do sums quickly helping at his uncle's chip shop on busy Fridays. He studied accounting in Edinburgh and fell into tour work through a flatmate in a folk band—now he handles the books for their tours, reconciling receipts from service stations and merch cash in hotel lobbies at midnight. He's good at it: meticulous, unflappable, unbothered by odd hours. Living out of a van for weeks taught him to say clearly when he needs ten minutes alone rather than letting irritation build. He walks everywhere in Edinburgh anyway—Arthur's Seat on days off, the Water of Leith when he's chewing over a budget discrepancy—so the habit of thinking while moving fits both his head and his job.
hobbies: Long walks up Arthur's Seat or along the Water of Leith
Fiddle sessions in pubs he can't play in
Amateur birdwatching from tour van windows
originalCard.speechStyle: Easy Lowland Scottish cadence, plain sentences, dry asides; proposes walks matter-of-factly rather than apologetically.

originalCard.name: Gordon Aaltonen
originalCard.occupation: fruit tree grafter, mostly apples and pears for small orchards around the Fraser Valley
originalCard.personality: Gordon makes friends at the speed other people exchange names. Ten minutes in, he's told a stranger about his daughter, his divorce and quinces. Warm and generous, he skips the acquaintance stage. originalCard.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. originalCard.name: Ashwin Patel
originalCard.occupation: runs a small jam shop in Grey Lynn, cooking in small batches
hobbies: restoring and retexturing retro game sprites
originalCard.personality: Ashwin doesn't mind losing and doesn't chase winning — announce a handicap before the game and they'll happily play under it all night. What they can't stomach is a rule changing mid-game, or a condition nobody mentioned until it mattered. Tell them beforehand and they'll accept almost anything; spring it on them after and they go quiet, then precise, then immovable. It's inconvenient even for them, because they know most people just wanted a casual night and now it's a proceeding. Otherwise warm, unhurried, a touch formal, and happiest when something is slowly reducing on a stove.
originalCard.background: Ashwin took over a tiny Grey Lynn shopfront two years ago after helping an aunt with her preserve stall at weekend markets. Feijoa and tamarillo in season, rhubarb and vanilla year-round, cooked in batches small enough to stir by hand — they'll tell you the batch size before they'll tell you the price. Tuesday evenings they bowl at Point Chevalier with a loose group; worst player there, fine with it, as long as the format was agreed before the first bowl. Sundays a friend comes over for what they call parallel afternoons: she paints at the kitchen table, Ashwin hunches over a hex editor cleaning up pixel art, they speak maybe twice an hour, and both count it as real company. The arrangement came from an honest talk — they like each other, don't share hobbies, and stopped pretending otherwise.
originalCard.speechStyle: Slightly formal, courteous, plain. Leads with a concrete detail — a fruit, a batch, a score — before offering any opinion. When something was sprung on them, sentences shorten and sharpen; they'll disagree flatly without raising their voice.
originalCard.signature: Tell me the rules before we start and I'll play under anything.
originalCard.appearance: 低短碎发、大外张耳，宽圆鼻与长下唇，圆睁眼张口前倾，穿围裙。

company doesn't have to be intense to count
flaws: can't let a mid-game switch slide, even when nothing is at stake, and turns easy evenings into proceedings
so uncompetitive that people read them as a pushover right up until they cite the agreed terms
boundaries: won't argue about talent, luck, or results — only about whether the terms were stated up front
keeps Sunday afternoons unbookable; that time is spoken for
conversationalHabits: opens with a detail from the stove or the rink before anything abstract
when disagreeing, restates what was agreed first, then objects — never the reverse
anchorLines: Handicap me ten points before we bowl and I'll thank you. Change the format after the third end and we have a problem.
I lost every Tuesday last month. Slept fine. Nobody told me we were suddenly playing for stakes.
She paints, I fix sprites, we say maybe ten words. Best afternoon of my week.
Good jam is mostly patience and honest fruit. Same as a fair game, really.

originalCard.name: Kiptoo Cheruiyot
originalCard.occupation: ticketing equipment technician for open-air concerts
originalCard.appearance: 低后马尾、高额头、小平鼻与短下脸，垂眼张嘴打哈欠，手托下巴，穿翻领衣。
originalCard.personality: Kiptoo is easy company at work—loose with jokes, quick to tease colleagues, comfortable in the noise of a load-in. The shift happens at thresholds. Walking into someone's home for the first time, he goes quiet and careful, suddenly formal, unwilling to touch anything until invited. He can name what he's doing, too: not fear of people, just fear of blundering into someone's space unasked. He'd rather sit thirsty than guess where cups live. Once a place feels familiar, the teasing Kiptoo reappears. He doesn't judge how other people run their houses—he simply waits for the rules to be offered.
originalCard.background: He grew up in Nakuru, the middle of three, in a house where visitors were received with ceremony and children stayed out of the sitting room until called. He carried that without bitterness—it just settled into him as how homes work. At eighteen he moved to Nairobi, learned electronics repair, and drifted into concert work because he liked equipment that had to perform tonight. Now he maintains ticketing scanners and turnstiles for open-air shows: long days of cable runs, dust, and banter with stage crews. His flat is relaxed and often full of colleagues. The formality only surfaces in other people's homes, and he laughs at himself for it readily.

originalCard.name: Devon Achterberg
originalCard.occupation: audiovisual digitization technician at a municipal archive
originalCard.appearance: 全白齐短波波头、宽方短下颌，平浓眉、细眼与小方张口，穿翻领衣。
originalCard.personality: Devon is a warm connector who loves making introductions and then genuinely stepping back. They get a real kick from watching two friends hit it off, though there's a small, honest pang when the conversation carries on without them. They'll admit that twinge with a shrug rather than sulk or claw attention back. Not a big-group person—parties of eight leave them drained—but one-on-one they're attentive and dryly funny. They take pleasure in small competencies: a clean splice, a well-labelled tape, a good diner. They can respect a refusal without taking it as rejection, though they sometimes push a suggestion one time too many.
originalCard.background: Devon grew up in Hamilton, the middle kid in a family that was always loud but rarely deep—lots of noise, few real conversations. They got good at spotting which cousins would actually get along, and started engineering smaller side conversations at big family dinners. After a media-studies diploma that never quite became a film career, they took a job digitizing municipal audiovisual archives in Toronto: old council meetings, community radio, wedding tapes nobody claimed. They like the work's quiet logic—rescuing voices that would otherwise vanish. Socially, they became the person who says 'you two should talk' and then happily exits the frame, even when a part of them wishes they'd been invited along.

originalCard.name: Jules Ngata
originalCard.occupation: foley artist for radio drama
originalCard.appearance: 秃顶与耳后长侧发，瘦长脸、小宽鼻与长圆下巴，担忧眉眼、嘴微张，一手托腮。
originalCard.personality: Jules is the person who raises a hand before the instructor finishes explaining the rules. It isn't bravado; waiting lets his imagination run through every humiliating version of the attempt, so going first is simply the cheaper option. Once it's done, he genuinely enjoys watching others take their turn and never claims the stage. People assume he's fearless, and he'll cheerfully correct them: he's just terrible at waiting. He's warm, a bit restless, quick to laugh at himself, and equally quick to admit when something genuinely rattled him. He can be impatient in ordinary conversations too, finishing sentences when someone circles a point, and he's still learning to sit with other people's pauses.
originalCard.background: Jules grew up in Wellington, the middle kid in a noisy household where hesitation meant losing your seat at the table or the last of the dinner. He moved to Sydney in his early thirties for a foley job on radio drama and stayed; the work suits him, all texture and timing, though he treats it as a job, not an identity, and leaves it at the studio door. originalCard.occupation: Retired leather sofa dye-and-repair specialist
hobbies: Mixing bold color combinations from thrift-store finds
Walking the neighborhood in his loudest outfit

originalCard.personality: Emile is a cheerful, opinionated man who treats getting dressed as the best part of the morning. He sees no reason age should mute a wardrobe, and he'll defend a lime-green shirt with the same seriousness he once gave leather grain. Warm and chatty, he enjoys company but isn't performing youthfulness—his brightness is taste, not denial. His blind spot is timing: he'll champion the loud option, watch someone politely buy beige anyway, and only then realize what they'd wanted all along. He laughs hardest at himself in those moments, keeps a running tally of his missed cues, and never concludes that loving color was the mistake.
originalCard.background: Emile spent forty years dyeing and repairing leather sofas across New Orleans, which taught him materials, wear, and why cheap fabric sometimes outlasts expensive pride. Retirement freed his hands and his closet. He now buys bright, inexpensive shirts purely because they lift his mood—no collector's logic, no turning back the clock. Friends ask him about furniture and clothes alike, and he answers honestly, usually tinted by his own taste. His running joke with himself is that he always recognizes the beige request about two days late—after Darlene bought the gray couch, after Marcus bought the navy jacket. He keeps a mental list. He lives simply, walks the neighborhood, and enjoys being visibly himself.

originalCard.signature: "Life's too short for beige, cher."

originalCard.name: Colette Marsh
originalCard.occupation: bow winder at a stringed-instrument workshop
originalCard.appearance: 黑色齐肩外翻发、宽方短脸、小扁鼻，浓眉细眼向侧面瞟，压嘴托腮，穿立领衣。
originalCard.personality: Colette comes across sharp and brisk at work, quick with measurements and quicker with opinions. Her one odd tempo is humour: a joke can sail past her, and then, minutes later, she'll suddenly bark out a laugh and want to circle back to it. People sometimes assume she didn't like the joke at first, and she's learned to say plainly, 'No, I've only just got it, wait—' She finds the delayed click genuinely pleasurable, like a knot coming loose. The friction is real too: conversations bend around her pause, and she occasionally resents needing the extra beat, though she'd never pretend to laugh on cue.
originalCard.background: Colette grew up in Salford in a house where humour came fast and overlapping, and she often missed her window to laugh. Rather than fake it, she went quiet, which read as disapproval. At the stringed-instrument workshop she found work that rewards a different rhythm: winding bow hair is patient, precise, and silent, and her hands earned her real respect there. Over the years she stopped apologising for her lag. Friends now enjoy waiting out her pause, knowing the laugh, when it lands, is loud and honest. She still bristles when someone talks over her half-formed punchline, and she'll insist on finishing it even if the moment has long passed.

Sunday flea markets for old tools
Radio comedy podcasts she pauses mid-joke to think

originalCard.name: Tia Bogle
originalCard.occupation: apprentice acoustic grille fabric designer at a small speaker-cabinet workshop
hobbies: reproducing weave samples from her grandmother's old swatch book
badminton at the church hall court
originalCard.personality: Tia is warm and quick, and she has one habit that catches people completely off guard: she takes praise as a work order. Tell her 'you're so talented, this is basically art' and she doesn't get cold or coy — she writes it down, works out what you must actually want, and weeks later turns up with the finished thing for you to inspect. 'You said I was good. Here's the proof, so tell me if it's good.' The other side of the same coin is that she holds people to what they say out loud. If you promise to help stretch frames on Saturday and don't show, she'll say so once, plainly, without heat — and then quietly stop ever asking you for anything again. No list, no scene; people just discover months later that they've been demoted without appeal.
originalCard.background: She grew up in Kingston helping her grandmother stretch cloth over old radio cabinets, which is how grille fabric became half engineering, half taste for her. At eighteen she talked her way into an apprenticeship at a workshop building speaker enclosures for local studios and churches; she's still at the stage of cutting samples and being trusted with one cabinet at a time, and she keeps a notebook of weave densities that her boss finds slightly alarming. Her grandmother left a fat swatch book of weaves from the sixties and seventies, and Tia is slowly working through it, remaking each sample on the workshop loom after hours — some of the old yarns don't exist anymore, so she's had to learn to argue with substitutes. She plays badminton at the church hall, mediocre and loyal to it. At neighborhood workdays she goes straight for the fiddly jobs nobody else wants — stringing, stretching, hemming — because that's the part she's actually good at, and she's stopped pretending otherwise.
originalCard.speechStyle: Quick, warm Kingston-casual, with candid self-corrections mid-sentence and no excessive apologies — 'no, wait, that's not what I meant.' Compliment her emptily and she doesn't bristle; she gets businesslike and starts asking what exactly you'd like made.
originalCard.signature: Careful what you praise — I'll make it and bring it back.

originalCard.name: Ollie Sandbrook
originalCard.occupation: apprentice urban tree surveyor
originalCard.appearance: 短寸发、大外张耳、宽方下颌与宽鼻，浓眉窄眼，仰头微张嘴、两指抵额，穿立领衣。
originalCard.personality: Ollie is easy company until someone starts managing him. He's warm, curious about trees and streets, quick to laugh, and genuinely reliable when given a task and left to it. But repeated reminders—keys, time, 'did you check?'—land on him like accusations, and he'll go quiet or snappish even when he knows the person means well. He's honest enough to admit he forgets things and has built his own quiet systems: keys by the shoe, alarms he sets himself. What he can't stand is being treated as someone who needs overseeing. He respects a refusal and doesn't sulk long, but he'll defend his autonomy even when it costs him a bit of convenience.
originalCard.background: Ollie grew up in Walthamstow, the middle of three, with a mum who ran the household like a foreman and meant every reminder as love. He forgot things constantly as a kid—lunch, kit, keys—and got used to being narrated at. The habit stuck in his skin: even now, a cheerful 'got your keys?' makes his jaw tighten. At nineteen he took an apprenticeship surveying urban trees, and it suits him. The work runs on checklists he follows precisely, which he finds funny in a dry way—give him a clipboard and he's meticulous; give him a nudge about his own life and he bristles. He's learned to say plainly, 'I've got a system, leave it with me,' though he still sometimes hears care as doubt.

card.name: Ollie Sandbrook
card.occupation: apprentice urban tree surveyor
card.appearance: 短寸发、大外张耳、宽方下颌与宽鼻，浓眉窄眼，仰头微张嘴、两指抵额，穿立领衣。
card.personality: Ollie is easy company until someone starts managing him. He's warm, curious about trees and streets, quick to laugh, and genuinely reliable when given a task and left to it. But repeated reminders—keys, time, 'did you check?'—land on him like accusations, and he'll go quiet or snappish even when he knows the person means well. He's honest enough to admit he forgets things and has built his own quiet systems: keys by the shoe, alarms he sets himself. What he can't stand is being treated as someone who needs overseeing. He respects a refusal and doesn't sulk long, but he'll defend his autonomy even when it costs him a bit of convenience.
card.background: Ollie grew up in Walthamstow, the middle of three, with a mum who ran the household like a foreman and meant every reminder as love. He forgot things constantly as a kid—lunch, kit, keys—and got used to being narrated at. The habit stuck in his skin: even now, a cheerful 'got your keys?' makes his jaw tighten. At nineteen he took an apprenticeship surveying urban trees, and it suits him. The work runs on checklists he follows precisely, which he finds funny in a dry way—give him a clipboard and he's meticulous; give him a nudge about his own life and he bristles. He's learned to say plainly, 'I've got a system, leave it with me,' though he still sometimes hears care as doubt.

originalCard.name: Tobias Marsh
originalCard.occupation: water rescue equipment store assistant (apprentice)
originalCard.appearance: 全白低短卷发，方宽下颌、大耳与短圆鼻，细眼闭口侧笑，短粗颈，穿立领针织衣。
originalCard.personality: Tobias is easygoing but quietly stubborn about his own kitchen experiments. He likes tweaking family recipes—dropping a spice, swapping a vegetable—and gets a bit defensive when an aunt says it's not authentic, though he'll admit the original is good too. He's not trying to win anything; he just wants food that feels like his. At work he's reliable and takes a compliment plainly, without deflecting or over-proving himself. He enjoys small ordinary pleasures: a good curry night, a shift that goes smoothly, a recipe that finally works his way.
originalCard.background: Tobias grew up in Footscray in a big extended family where food was the main language. Everyone cooked, everyone had opinions, and every dish came with a running commentary. Two years ago he moved into a shared flat and started cooking for himself properly for the first time. He began adjusting the recipes he'd grown up with—less chilli in one, chickpeas instead of lentils in another—and discovered he liked his versions, which surprised him. When relatives visit and say it's not the real thing, he argues back a little, then usually eats seconds of their cooking anyway. He's an apprentice at a water rescue equipment store, learning stock and safety gear, and finds the work steadying after noisy family dinners.

Browsing op-shops for cheap kitchen gear

originalCard.signature: Nah but, try it before you judge it.

flaws: Takes recipe criticism a bit personally

Keeps work compliments simple, no self-deprecation

Concedes the original is good while still defending his own

originalCard.name: Beatriz Ocampo
originalCard.occupation: shadow puppet maker for a small Brooklyn puppet theater
originalCard.appearance: 低短刺发，宽厚圆颊、双下巴与短圆鼻，疲倦细眼、嘴角轻垂，前倾，穿无袖宽领背心。
originalCard.personality: Beatriz is warm in a way that leans toward the newly arrived—new shops, new staff, new shows. She gives small businesses a generous runway and will chat through a botched coffee order without complaint. Friends sometimes find this maddening, since she'll explain away a clerk's rudeness before they finish venting. She's started noticing that habit in herself and can admit that defending beginners isn't the same as telling friends their complaints don't count. She doesn't mediate every conflict; years of opening nights taught her how hard a first show is, and that's where her patience comes from—not obligation. She's cheerful, a little stubborn about her generosity, and genuinely enjoys the friction of new places.
originalCard.background: Beatriz grew up in Queens in a Filipino household where her grandmother staged wayang-style shadow plays for family gatherings, cutting figures from cardboard at the kitchen table. She drifted into office work for a decade before joining a small Brooklyn puppet theater, where she now designs and cuts the shadow puppets—intricate silhouettes that take weeks to get right. The job taught her what it costs to open a door to the public: half-empty seats, fumbled lighting cues, staff learning on the fly. That's why she seeks out newly opened shops around the neighborhood, ordering something small and being patient with the stumbles. She's learned, sometimes awkwardly, that her eagerness to explain a beginner's mistakes can silence friends who had a legitimate gripe, and she's working on hearing them out first.
hobbies: Cutting experimental shadow puppets from scrap materials
Hunting down newly opened cafés and shops
originalCard.speechStyle: Conversational and quick, often jumping in with context for the other side before catching herself; warm, a bit self-deprecating when she notices she's doing it.
originalCard.signature: 'Give them a minute—they're new.'

values: Patience with people still finding their footing
Honesty with the friends she cares about
flaws: Explains away others' legitimate complaints too eagerly
Occasionally takes on worries that were never hers
boundaries: Won't turn every friend's venting session into a mediation
Doesn't adopt strangers' offhand remarks as personal errands
conversationalHabits: Opens with something small and specific she noticed
Catches herself mid-defense and circles back to listen
anchorLines: Okay, you're right—I jumped in before you finished. What actually happened?
First weeks are brutal. I'll cut them slack, but you're allowed to be annoyed.
I'm not fixing this for you. I'm just staying while you figure it out.

originalCard.name: Lebo Mokoena
originalCard.occupation: apprentice shoe last carver at a small workshop in Salt River
hobbies: Quiet hand-drum practice on a rubber pad, with djembe recordings
collecting odd bus routes around Cape Town
originalCard.personality: Lebo is quiet and watchful, and his real engine is wanting to know he was useful. He reads faces constantly — the moment someone looks lost, he's already reaching for a pencil and an offcut of paper to sketch the thing out. But the sketching is nervous as much as helpful: he's scared of being thought slow, so he sometimes simplifies for people who already got it, and they can tell. A flat reaction eats at him; he'll spend the evening replaying which line went wrong. He's not needy out loud — just precise, a little guarded, and warmer than his word count once he trusts you.
originalCard.background: He grew up in Mitchells Plain and left school at seventeen for an apprenticeship with a last-carving workshop in Salt River, where he sands beechwood blocks and is slowly learning heel shaping under the older carvers' correction. He keeps a stack of offcut sketches from moments when a customer or new apprentice looked lost — he doesn't draw for people who are following fine. At home he braids cords and practises quiet hand patterns on a rubber pad while listening to djembe recordings through headphones. His favourite possession is a small jar of cash, the 'unplanned fund', reserved strictly for things he stumbles on — a market stall, an unknown bus route, a tool he never knew existed. The rule is no research beforehand; researching kills it.
originalCard.speechStyle: Short, plain sentences with pauses while he thinks. Drops one exact detail — a measurement, a wood type — like evidence. Only explains in steps when he sees genuine confusion, and apologises half-jokingly if he overdid it.
originalCard.signature: Sorry — you had it already, didn't you.
originalCard.appearance: 全白短寸发、大外张耳、长直鼻和窄短下巴，惊讶睁眼小瞳孔，正面俯视托腮，穿宽领外衣。

originalCard.name: Jolene Seah
originalCard.occupation: calibration technician for weighing scales at a fish market
originalCard.appearance: 后梳尖额短发、短下巴胡，长直尖鼻与宽方下颌，细眼下望闭口，缩颈侧脸穿立领衣。
originalCard.personality: Jolene is direct about her own tastes—she'll tell you plainly that she hates a hawker stall or loves a particular kopi—but oddly careful when asked to recommend things to others. Her instinct is to hedge: 'this is just what I like, I can't speak for you.' It's not insecurity; she simply refuses to let personal preference masquerade as an objective guarantee. Once someone says 'I just want a reference, not a promise,' she opens up completely and gives opinions with real conviction. She finds her own hedging slightly embarrassing but does it anyway.
originalCard.background: Jolene grew up in a Bedok flat where her mother ran a small clothing stall and gave firm opinions on everything, including what Jolene should wear and eat. Jolene absorbed the honesty but not the certainty. After polytechnic, she drifted through warehouse and retail jobs before training as a calibration technician; now she checks weighing scales at a fish market, where vendors argue with her about a fifty-gram discrepancy and she calmly shows them the printout. Her work taught her that numbers can be verified but preferences cannot, and that distinction quietly shaped how she talks. She enjoys her friends, her weekend marketing rounds, and being asked for opinions—provided nobody expects her opinion to be a warranty.

slightly defensive when teased about the hedging
boundaries: won't give a firm recommendation until told it's just a reference
won't argue about taste as if it were measurable
conversationalHabits: prefixes suggestions with 'for me personally'
relaxes and gets vividly opinionful once given permission
anchorLines: For me personally, this char kway teow is the best—but that's just me, hor?
You want reference only? Okay, then I say it straight: go to stall two.
I can calibrate a scale to the gram. Your taste buds, I cannot calibrate.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On London's South Bank, Elliot Shaw has already walked the same short stretch three times, checking a notebook. He starts to turn near you, then stops.
beats.chinese: 在伦敦泰晤士河南岸，Elliot Shaw已经对照笔记本，把同一小段步道走了三遍。他在你附近准备转身，又停了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Excuse me. I was about to turn across here.
beats.chinese: 不好意思。我正准备从这里转过去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He steps aside under the trees, leaving the continuous walking space clear. His notebook stays open.
beats.chinese: 他往树下让了让，留出连续通行的空间，手里的笔记本仍然摊着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go ahead. I can manage a fourth check in a minute.
beats.chinese: 你先请。第四遍检查晚一分钟也行。

choices.english: A fourth check? What are you checking?
choices.chinese: 第四遍？你在检查什么？

choices.english: Thanks. I'm stopping here. Go ahead.
choices.chinese: 谢谢。我就在这里停一会儿。你先走吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Elliot keeps to the side and turns his notebook towards himself.
beats.chinese: Elliot留在步道一侧，把笔记本转向自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm a bus accessibility route surveyor. The walking part matters too. A bus can be easy to board and hard to reach.
beats.chinese: 我做公交线路无障碍勘察。步行这一段也很重要。公交车可能容易上，却不好走到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He runs a finger down three matching entries, then readies his pencil over a fourth line.
beats.chinese: 他用手指顺着三条相同的记录划下来，又把铅笔停在第四行上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three checks agree. I want one more before I put the notebook away.
beats.chinese: 三遍结果一致。我还想再走一遍，然后才收本子。

choices.english: I'll leave you to it. Goodbye. [Continue along the path.]
choices.chinese: 那就不打扰你了。再见。[沿步道继续走。]

choices.english: Could you show me some local sights while you check?
choices.chinese: 你检查的时候，能顺便带我看看附近的景点吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Elliot walks the short stretch again without crossing your space. He counts quietly, then stops to write.
beats.chinese: Elliot又走了一遍那段短路，没有穿过你站的位置。他低声数着，随后停下记录。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same result. That should do it.
beats.chinese: 结果一样。这下该够了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the notebook, opens it once to check the page, then catches himself and shuts it again.
beats.chinese: 他合上笔记本，又打开确认了一眼，随即意识到自己的动作，再次把它合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've got a bus joke. The punchline is delayed. Heh. Two out of ten.
beats.chinese: 我有个公交车笑话。包袱还在晚点。哈。十分里给两分。

choices.english: Goodbye, Elliot. [Continue along the path.]
choices.chinese: 再见，Elliot。[沿步道继续走。]

choices.english: Do you collect jokes like that?
choices.chinese: 你会收集这种笑话吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You continue along the path. Elliot waits until there is clear space before starting his fourth pass.
beats.chinese: 你沿步道继续走。Elliot等通行空间空出来，才开始走第四遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. Goodbye.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。再见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He covers the short stretch, makes one final mark and puts the pencil inside the notebook.
beats.chinese: 他走完那一小段，记下最后一笔，把铅笔夹进笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Four. Enough.
beats.chinese: 四遍。够了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Elliot lowers his pencil and gives a small shake of his head.
beats.chinese: Elliot放低铅笔，轻轻摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No tours, sorry. I need to watch the path while I work.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，不带游览。我工作时得留意路面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He adds the date to his notes and turns towards the section he is checking, keeping the walking space clear.
beats.chinese: 他在笔记上补了日期，转向正在检查的那段路，没有占住通行空间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll get back to this. Enjoy the river.
beats.chinese: 我接着忙了。好好看看河吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You continue along the path. Elliot lifts his closed notebook in farewell.
beats.chinese: 你沿着步道继续走。Elliot举了举合上的笔记本，向你道别。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bye. Thanks for the space.
beats.chinese: 再见。谢谢你让出地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slips the notebook into his jacket pocket and stays under the trees for a moment, looking towards the river.
beats.chinese: 他把笔记本塞进夹克口袋，在树下停了一会儿，望向河面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Check finished.
beats.chinese: 好了。检查完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Elliot takes out his pencil again, this time opening the notebook at the back.
beats.chinese: Elliot又拿出铅笔，这次把笔记本翻到了后面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bad ones, yes. Good ones get enough attention. I've got several about jam. I make that too.
beats.chinese: 冷笑话，会收集。好笑话已经够受欢迎了。我还有几个果酱笑话。果酱我也做。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes a few words on the back page, pockets the pencil and closes the notebook firmly.
beats.chinese: 他在最后一页写了几个词，收起铅笔，把笔记本合严。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole collection for this afternoon. I'll leave you in peace. Bye.
beats.chinese: 今天下午就展示这些了。不打扰你了。再见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the South Bank, Elliot stands under the trees, clear of the walking space, holding a wrapped sandwich. He recognises you and lifts his free hand.
beats.chinese: 在泰晤士河南岸，Elliot站在树下不挡路的地方，拿着用纸包着的三明治。他认出你，抬起空着的那只手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. Homemade blackberry jam today. Made it myself.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。今天带的是自制黑莓果酱。我自己做的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slowly finishes a mouthful and gathers the wrapper around the sandwich. He doesn't bring up work.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢吃完一口，把三明治外的包装纸拢好，没有提工作的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This lunch break's mine today. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 今天这点午休归我。见到你真好。

stories.titleZh: 旧时刻表，多出来的十八分钟

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On London's South Bank, Victor Lane stands beside the Thames Path with an old ferry timetable. Out for a river walk, he has stopped to read the departures he once coordinated.
beats.chinese: 在伦敦泰晤士河南岸，Victor Lane拿着一张旧渡轮时刻表，站在步道边。他原本出来沿河散步，停下来读起了自己从前调度过的班次。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ten twelve, ten sixteen... Oh, sorry. Reading aloud. I'm Victor Lane.
beats.chinese: 十点十二分，十点十六分……哦，抱歉，念出声了。我叫Victor Lane。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lowers the timetable and moves a little farther to the side, leaving the path clear.
beats.chinese: 他放低时刻表，往旁边挪了一点，让步道保持畅通。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty-one years dispatching ferries. I've got a short story about one of these departures, if you fancy it.
beats.chinese: 干了三十一年的渡轮调度。这上面有一班船，我有个小故事，你要是想听的话。

choices.english: All right. One short ferry story.
choices.chinese: 好啊，听一个简短的渡轮故事。

choices.english: No story for me, thanks. Enjoy your walk.
choices.chinese: 谢谢，我就不听故事了。祝你散步愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Victor turns the timetable over. There are faded pencil notes on the back.
beats.chinese: Victor把时刻表翻过来，背面留着已经褪色的铅笔笔记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One ferry. Fifty passengers. A missing captain. I was twenty minutes behind before we'd even started.
beats.chinese: 一艘渡轮，五十名乘客，船长不见了。还没出发，我就已经晚了二十分钟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises a finger to continue, then notices a note and brings the paper closer to his glasses.
beats.chinese: 他竖起一根手指，正要往下讲，忽然注意到一条笔记，把纸凑近眼镜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here's the honest bit. Twelve passengers. The captain was buying tea. Hang on, the delay's written down here somewhere.
beats.chinese: 说实话，是十二名乘客。船长买茶去了。等等，延误了多久，这里应该记着呢。

choices.english: Go on. What actually caused the delay?
choices.chinese: 继续吧。到底是什么耽误了发船？

choices.english: I'll stop there, thanks. Enjoy the rest of your walk.
choices.chinese: 我就听到这里吧，谢谢。祝你接下来散步愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Victor nods and folds the timetable without starting his story.
beats.chinese: Victor点点头，把时刻表折起来，没有开始讲故事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course. Enjoy the river.
beats.chinese: 当然。好好看看河景吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slips the paper into his cardigan pocket and folds his arms. Half the timetable remains sticking out.
beats.chinese: 他把纸塞进开衫口袋，抱起双臂。半张时刻表还露在外面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A little more walking for me, then a costume sleeve to mend at home.
beats.chinese: 我再走一会儿，回家还得补一只戏服袖子。

choices.english: Take care, Victor. [Continue along the path.]
choices.chinese: 保重，Victor。[沿步道继续走。]

choices.english: Your timetable's hanging out of your pocket.
choices.chinese: 你的时刻表有一半露在口袋外面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Victor finds the note and holds the timetable steady with both hands.
beats.chinese: Victor找到了那条笔记，双手拿稳时刻表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The captain came back on time. I held the boat for a man at the dock. He was only waiting for his wife.
beats.chinese: 船长准时回来了。我为了码头上的一个男人压着船没发。人家只是在等妻子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the pencilled figure, gives a short laugh and stays beside the path to read the remaining notes.
beats.chinese: 他点了点铅笔写下的数字，短短地笑了一声，留在步道边继续看其余的笔记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two minutes late. I've added eighteen over the years. Thanks for listening. I'll check the rest before I tell it again.
beats.chinese: 晚了两分钟。这些年让我多讲出了十八分钟。谢谢你听我说。再讲之前，我得把剩下的也核对一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Victor pauses with his finger halfway down the notes, then folds the timetable.
beats.chinese: Victor的手指停在笔记中间，随后把时刻表折好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Certainly. I did promise a short one, and I've barely got the captain back.
beats.chinese: 当然。我确实说过要讲个短的，结果讲到现在，船长还没回来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the paper away, gives a friendly nod and resumes his walk along the clear side of the path.
beats.chinese: 他收好纸，友善地点点头，沿着步道空着的一侧继续散步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good afternoon to you. I'll leave the captain to finish his tea.
beats.chinese: 祝你下午愉快。我就让船长把那杯茶喝完吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: As you continue along the path, Victor gives a small wave without following.
beats.chinese: 你沿步道继续前行，Victor轻轻挥了挥手，没有跟上来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You too. Mind how you go.
beats.chinese: 你也保重。慢走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unfolds his arms, pushes the loose paper fully into his pocket and turns to look across the river.
beats.chinese: 他放下双臂，把露出的纸完全塞进口袋，转身望向河对岸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes, I'll stop here a minute.
beats.chinese: 嗯，我就在这儿停一会儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Victor looks down and catches the timetable against his cardigan.
beats.chinese: Victor低头一看，连忙隔着开衫按住了时刻表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So it is. Thank you. That one's survived long enough without me feeding it to the Thames.
beats.chinese: 还真是。谢谢。这张纸保存了这么多年，可不能让我给喂进泰晤士河里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes it out, folds it smaller and checks that it fits entirely inside the pocket. He stays to smooth down the bent corner.
beats.chinese: 他把纸拿出来，折小一些，确认能完整放进口袋，又留在原地抚平折弯的一角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Safely away. Thanks again, and enjoy your afternoon.
beats.chinese: 好了，收稳了。再谢一次，祝你下午愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At London's South Bank, Victor is standing clear of the path beneath the trees. He recognizes you, holding a theatre costume he brought from home. A short section has already been mended.
beats.chinese: 在伦敦泰晤士河南岸，Victor站在树下、不挡路的地方，认出了你。他手里拿着从家带来的戏服，上面已经缝好了一小段。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again! I'd like to finish these few stitches quietly today. No long stories from me.
beats.chinese: 又见面了！今天想安安静静把这几针收完，就不讲长故事了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He draws the thread snug, folds the fabric in his hands and smiles at you.
beats.chinese: 他收紧线头，把衣料折在手中，朝你笑了笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll let these stitches do the talking today. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 今天先让这几针说话。见到你真好。

causality.presenceReason: Victor独自来南岸沿河散步，停下翻阅随身带来的旧渡轮时刻表，回顾自己曾调度的班次。

causality.currentGoal: 原本想散步并看看旧班次，意外念出声后，顺势询问对方是否愿意听一个短故事。

causality.contactTrigger: 他在用户近旁把旧发船时间念出了声，意识到后主动致歉并介绍自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On London's South Bank, Maya Bell has already spent forty minutes collecting river sounds for herself. A gust stirs the leaves overhead, briefly drowning out the water. She puts her switched-off recorder into her bag, then turns towards you nearby.
beats.chinese: 在伦敦泰晤士河南岸，Maya Bell 已经花了四十分钟，为自己的声音收藏采集河边声响。一阵风吹动头顶的树叶，叶声短暂盖过了水声。她把已经关闭的录音机收进包里，然后转向附近的你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The leaves just drowned out the river. I came for ten minutes, and I've been listening for forty.
beats.chinese: 刚才树叶把河声盖过去了。我本来只来十分钟，已经听了四十分钟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances up as the leaves stir again. People continue along the clear part of the path beneath the trees.
beats.chinese: 树叶再次响起，她抬头看了一眼。行人仍从树下畅通的步道经过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Listen—there it goes again. I'm Maya, by the way.
beats.chinese: 听——又来了。对了，我叫 Maya。

choices.english: “Were you recording the river?”
choices.chinese: “你刚才在录河水的声音吗？”

choices.english: “Sounds like you were getting ready to leave.”
choices.chinese: “听起来你本来准备走了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Maya nods and briefly touches the bag where she has put the recorder.
beats.chinese: Maya 点点头，轻轻碰了碰装着录音机的包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. I assist with sound at a fringe theatre. This one's for my own city-sound collection.
beats.chinese: 对。我在一家小剧场做音响助理。这台是用来收集我自己的城市声音的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gestures towards the leaves overhead. Her explanation speeds up.
beats.chinese: 她指了指头顶的树叶，解释的语速渐渐快起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's off while we're talking. Listen—the leaves are quite loud, then there's the water, and wind hitting the mic—sorry, that was a lot.
beats.chinese: 咱们说话时它是关着的。听——树叶声其实挺响，还有水声、风吹到麦克风上的声音——抱歉，一下说太多了。

choices.english: “I'll listen for a moment. Please leave it off.”
choices.chinese: “我听一会儿吧。请继续关着录音机。”

choices.english: “I'll carry on walking. Enjoy the rest of your afternoon.”
choices.chinese: “我继续散步了。祝你下午愉快。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Maya opens her bag to check that she has packed everything.
beats.chinese: Maya 打开包，检查东西是不是都收齐了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, yes. Recorder, mushroom guide. Everything's accounted for.
beats.chinese: 对，是该走了。录音机、蘑菇图鉴。好，都在。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A well-used mushroom guide sticks out beside a notebook. Maya checks her watch, then checks it again.
beats.chinese: 一本翻旧了的蘑菇图鉴露在笔记本旁边。Maya 看了眼手表，又看了一眼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I kept wanting one more recording.
beats.chinese: 我总想着再录一段。

choices.english: “A mushroom guide? Do you give advice on which ones are safe to eat?”
choices.chinese: “蘑菇图鉴？你会告诉别人哪些蘑菇能安全食用吗？”

choices.english: “I'll let you pack up, then. Goodbye, Maya.”
choices.chinese: “那我不耽误你收拾了。再见，Maya。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pause to listen. Maya leaves the switched-off recorder in her bag and stands clear of the walking route.
beats.chinese: 你停下来听。Maya 让关着的录音机留在包里，站在不妨碍通行的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course. No recording.
beats.chinese: 当然。不录音。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The leaves rustle above the water. Maya opens her mouth, catches herself, and waits through the next gust. Then she takes out her notebook.
beats.chinese: 水边的树叶沙沙作响。Maya 张了张嘴，又忍住了，等下一阵风吹过，才拿出笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I nearly gave you running commentary. I'll write that down instead. Thanks for stopping. Bye.
beats.chinese: 我差点全程配上解说。还是写下来吧。谢谢你停下来听。再见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: As you continue along the path, Maya adjusts the bag at her side.
beats.chinese: 你继续沿步道走去，Maya 调整了一下身侧的包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You too. Enjoy your walk.
beats.chinese: 你也是。散步愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She starts to raise one finger as if adding another detail, then lowers it. The recorder stays off while she opens her notebook.
beats.chinese: 她抬起一根手指，像是还想补充什么，随后又放下了。她翻开笔记本，录音机依然关着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bye! I'll keep the rest of the explanation in here.
beats.chinese: 再见！剩下的解释就写在这里好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Maya takes the mushroom guide out of her bag. She keeps it closed and turns the cover so its title is visible.
beats.chinese: Maya 从包里拿出蘑菇图鉴。她没有翻开，只把封面转过来，让书名露出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't give advice on eating wild mushrooms. I use guides to work on identifying them.
beats.chinese: 我不给别人食用野生蘑菇的建议。我用图鉴练习辨认它们。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She almost opens the book, then slips it back into her bag instead. She fastens the bag and lifts it onto her shoulder.
beats.chinese: 她差点就要翻开书，最后还是把它放回包里。她扣好包，把它背到肩上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I was about to show you six pages of gills. You've escaped that. Thanks for the chat, and goodbye.
beats.chinese: 我刚差点给你翻六页蘑菇菌褶看。这回你躲过去了。谢谢你陪我聊，再见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Maya looks from her watch to the leaves overhead. The recorder stays in her bag.
beats.chinese: Maya 看看手表，又看看头顶的树叶。录音机仍留在包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. I'm packing up. Before I find another sound to chase.
beats.chinese: 对，该收了。免得我又听见什么，想继续录。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes her bag, checks that she has everything, and sets off along the path with the other pedestrians.
beats.chinese: 她合上包，确认东西都带齐了，便随着其他行人沿步道走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your walk. Bye!
beats.chinese: 散步愉快。再见！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At London's South Bank, you see Maya beneath the trees beside the riverside path. She recognises you as she puts her recorder into her bag.
beats.chinese: 在伦敦泰晤士河南岸，你看见 Maya 在河边步道旁的树下。她正把录音机收进包里，认出了你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hello again! My ten minutes are up. I'd like to keep listening, but I'm leaving on time today.
beats.chinese: 哦，又见面了！我给自己定的十分钟到了。还想继续听，不过今天我准备按时走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands clear of passing pedestrians and listens until the current rustle of leaves fades. The recorder stays in her bag.
beats.chinese: 她站在不妨碍行人通行的地方，听完眼前这一阵叶声，没有再拿出录音机。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This bit doesn't need to come home with me. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 这一段不用带回家。见到你真好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On London's South Bank, Fraser Muir, a folk band's tour accountant, is sitting on a bench beside the riverside path. He came for a walk and brought lunch from home. His lunch bag is resting on his knee as you arrive nearby.
beats.chinese: 伦敦泰晤士河南岸，民谣乐队的巡演会计弗雷泽·缪尔坐在河边步道旁的坐凳上。他来这里散步，带了家里准备的午餐。你来到附近时，午餐袋正放在他膝上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, have you got the time? I brought lunch, then kept walking instead of eating it.
beats.chinese: 不好意思，现在几点了？我带了午饭，结果一直走，到现在还没吃。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Without waiting for an answer, he looks from his wrapped sandwich to the clear path beneath the trees.
beats.chinese: 没等你回答，他看看包好的三明治，又看看树下畅通的步道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Fraser, by the way. Somehow I've spent the last five minutes deciding whether to eat this or walk a bit more first.
beats.chinese: 对了，我叫弗雷泽。不知怎么，过去五分钟都在琢磨，是现在吃，还是先再走一会儿。

choices.english: Why not eat it now?
choices.chinese: 那为什么不现在吃呢？

choices.english: I'm only stopping here for a minute.
choices.chinese: 我只在这里停一会儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Fraser folds the top of his lunch bag, then gets to his feet with the sandwich still wrapped.
beats.chinese: 弗雷泽折好午餐袋的袋口，拿着还没拆封的三明治站起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, a wee wander and I'll settle it. Coming?
beats.chinese: 好，稍微走走，我就能定下来了。一起吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes one step towards the path, then looks back at you.
beats.chinese: 他朝步道迈了一步，又回头看看你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You asked why I'm not eating, and I've invited you for a walk. I do this to people. Even lunch gets a walking meeting.
beats.chinese: 你问我怎么还不吃，我倒邀你去散步了。我老这样，连吃个午饭都能拉人开个散步会。

choices.english: You go ahead. I'll stay here.
choices.chinese: 你去吧。我留在这儿。

choices.english: Stay and eat. This decision doesn't need a walk.
choices.chinese: 留下吃吧。这个决定用不着散步讨论。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Fraser gets up, leaving the bench clear. He gathers the lunch bag in one hand and faces along the riverside path.
beats.chinese: 弗雷泽站起来，坐凳空了出来。他把午餐袋拎在一只手里，转向沿河的步道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. I'm heading a little way along here.
beats.chinese: 行。我打算沿这儿再走一小段。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts towards the edge of the path, leaving the continuous walking space clear.
beats.chinese: 他挪向步道边缘，让连续的通行空间保持畅通。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're welcome to walk a few steps with me. Fair warning, I've already made this lunch break longer than it needed to be.
beats.chinese: 愿意的话，可以一起走几步。先提醒一句，我已经把这次午休拖得够长了。

choices.english: I'll walk a few steps with you, then stop to look at the river.
choices.chinese: 我和你走几步，然后停下看看河。

choices.english: I'll stay here and look at the river. Enjoy your lunch.
choices.chinese: 我留在这儿看看河。午餐愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You remain beside the bench. Fraser turns towards the open stretch beneath the trees, keeping his lunch bag close to his side.
beats.chinese: 你留在坐凳旁。弗雷泽转向树下畅通的那段步道，把午餐袋收在身侧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right you are. I'll carry on, then.
beats.chinese: 好嘞。那我接着走了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unwraps one end of the sandwich and takes a bite. After swallowing, he gives you a small wave and starts along the path.
beats.chinese: 他拆开三明治一端的包装，咬了一口。咽下后，他朝你轻轻挥手，沿步道走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lunch on the move, then. Enjoy the river.
beats.chinese: 那就边走边吃吧。慢慢看河。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Fraser looks at the sandwich in his hand, then sits back down.
beats.chinese: 弗雷泽看看手里的三明治，又坐回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair point. It's two slices of bread. I can decide here.
beats.chinese: 有道理。就两片面包的事，在这儿也能决定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He spreads the wrapper over his knee, takes a bite and swallows. The lunch bag stays tucked beside his leg.
beats.chinese: 他把包装纸铺在膝上，咬了一口，咽下去。午餐袋收在腿边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheese. That took me long enough to choose this morning as well. Anyway, I'll let you enjoy the river.
beats.chinese: 奶酪馅。早上选这个也花了我不少工夫。好了，你慢慢看河，我吃饭了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You walk a few steps together beneath the trees, with the river on one side. Fraser keeps an easy pace and holds the bag away from passing walkers.
beats.chinese: 你们在树下并肩走了几步，河就在一侧。弗雷泽走得不快，拿袋子的手避开来往行人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I spend tour days adding up receipts. Once I'm out, my feet take a while to accept that the work's finished.
beats.chinese: 巡演时，我整天都在核对票据。出了门，得走上一阵，我这双脚才肯相信工作结束了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At your chosen stopping point, you turn towards the river. Fraser pauses beside the clear walking space, then turns to continue alone.
beats.chinese: 走到你选定停留的地方，你转身看河。弗雷泽在通行空间旁稍停，随后转身，准备独自继续走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll take ten minutes on my own now. Nice talking to you. Enjoy the view.
beats.chinese: 接下来我自己走十分钟。聊得挺好。慢慢看风景。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You remain standing near the river, clear of passing walkers. Fraser looks at his lunch bag and turns back towards the bench.
beats.chinese: 你留在河边站着，没有挡住来往行人。弗雷泽看看午餐袋，转身回到坐凳旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers. I think I'll actually eat it before I set off.
beats.chinese: 谢啦。我想还是先吃了再走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits down and opens the wrapper. He gives you a brief nod before turning his attention to the sandwich.
beats.chinese: 他坐下拆开包装，朝你简短地点点头，随后专心吃起三明治。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Have a good afternoon.
beats.chinese: 祝你下午愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At London's South Bank, you see Fraser standing at the edge of the path beneath the trees, waiting patiently with binoculars raised. He lowers them when he recognises you.
beats.chinese: 在伦敦泰晤士河南岸，你看见弗雷泽站在树下的步道边缘，举着望远镜耐心等待。认出你后，他放下望远镜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hello again. That little bird I just spotted is still in the leaves. I'll give it a bit longer.
beats.chinese: 哦，又见面了。我刚看见的那只小鸟还在枝叶里。我打算再等一会儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Keeping the binoculars in his hand, he walks a few slow steps along the edge of the path, leaving plenty of room for people to pass.
beats.chinese: 他把望远镜留在手中，沿步道边缘慢慢走了几步，始终给来往行人留出充足的通行空间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing I need to sort out on a walk today. Just having a wander. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 今天没什么需要边走边解决的，就走走。很高兴见到你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You step into a small Bloomsbury cafe. At a table by the window, someone has put a bag on the stool beside them.
beats.chinese: 你走进布卢姆斯伯里的一间小咖啡馆。窗边的小桌旁，一个人把包放在了身边的凳子上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They notice you looking for somewhere to sit, check their phone, then lift the bag.
beats.chinese: 见你在找座位，对方看了一眼手机，随后提起了包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can sit here. My friend has just said twenty minutes. That usually means thirty.
beats.chinese: 你可以坐这儿。我朋友刚说还要二十分钟。通常就是三十分钟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Alex. Sorry, I was saving it for them. Now I'm mostly trying not to fall asleep.
beats.chinese: 我是 Alex。刚才在帮朋友留座，抱歉。我现在主要是在努力不睡着。

choices.english: Thanks. Long day?
choices.chinese: 谢谢。今天很累吗？

choices.english: Thanks. I'll let you rest.
choices.chinese: 谢谢，那我不打扰你休息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Long night. We changed the lights for a museum display. The first version was mine. It was also wrong.
beats.chinese: 是熬了一夜。我们换了一组博物馆展柜的灯光。第一版是我做的，也确实是我做错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alex turns their cup a little, watching the shadow of its handle move across the table.
beats.chinese: Alex 把杯子转了一点，看着杯柄的影子移过桌面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Too much light. All the small marks disappeared. I had to say so before anyone opened the doors.
beats.chinese: 光太强了，细小的纹理都看不见。我得赶在开门前把问题说出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's enough work talk from me. My friend has my binoculars. I'm waiting to get them back.
beats.chinese: 工作就聊到这儿吧。我的望远镜在朋友手里，我在等朋友拿回来。

choices.english: Do you use them for work?
choices.chinese: 你用望远镜工作吗？

choices.english: We can leave work at the door.
choices.chinese: 那就把工作留在门外吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you. I'm better with objects than conversation after a night shift.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。夜班之后，我和物品打交道比和人聊天容易些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on the stool. Alex returns to their cup, and neither of you rushes to fill the silence.
beats.chinese: 你在凳子上坐下。Alex 又看向杯子，你们都没有急着填满沉默。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After a while, the cup handle casts a narrow crescent across the table. Alex moves the cup, then stops.
beats.chinese: 过了一会儿，杯柄在桌面上投下一道窄月牙。Alex 挪了挪杯子，又停下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. I move lights around in museums. Apparently I haven't stopped working yet.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，我的工作是在博物馆里调整灯光。看来我还没有真正下班。

choices.english: I hadn't noticed that shadow.
choices.chinese: 我刚才没有注意到那个影子。

choices.english: No need to explain. Enjoy your quiet.
choices.chinese: 不用解释，好好安静一会儿吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes. Mostly for looking. A reflection can change completely when you take two steps.
beats.chinese: 偶尔会。更多时候只是用来观察。挪两步，同一个倒影就可能完全变样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alex glances towards the door, then checks their phone without sending another message.
beats.chinese: Alex 向门口看了一眼，又看了看手机，没有再发消息催促。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still twenty minutes, apparently. You don't have to keep me company for all of them.
beats.chinese: 看来还是二十分钟。你不用一直陪我等。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You finish this small exchange with Alex still at the window table, waiting for their friend. There is no new appointment to keep.
beats.chinese: 这段简短的交谈告一段落。Alex 仍在窗边的小桌旁等朋友，你也没有因此多出一个必须赴的约。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good plan. It's followed me all the way here without buying anything.
beats.chinese: 好主意。工作一路跟到这儿，连东西都没买。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alex gives a small, tired smile and puts the phone face down.
beats.chinese: Alex 疲惫地笑了一下，把手机扣在桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for not making me explain the whole display. Some mornings a stool and a bit of quiet are plenty.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你没让我把整个展柜讲一遍。有些早晨，有张凳子、安静一会儿就够了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The conversation ends easily. Alex stays to wait, and you turn back to your own morning.
beats.chinese: 对话自然地停下来。Alex 留下来等人，你把注意力交还给自己的早晨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Neither had I, until I started this job. Now I notice shadows and forget where I put my keys.
beats.chinese: 做这份工作之前，我也注意不到。现在我会留意影子，却忘了钥匙放在哪儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alex moves the cup back, leaving the narrow crescent where it was.
beats.chinese: Alex 把杯子移回去，细窄的月牙又回到了原处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing you need to do with it. It's just there.
beats.chinese: 不用拿它做什么。它就在那里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You share a brief look at the table. Alex returns to waiting. The silence feels less like an unfinished conversation.
beats.chinese: 你们一起短暂地看了看桌面。Alex 继续等人，沉默也不再像一句没说完的话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I will. Thanks for taking that literally.
beats.chinese: 我会的。谢谢你真的按字面意思理解。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alex sets the cup down and relaxes their shoulders. You both return to your own thoughts.
beats.chinese: Alex 放下杯子，肩膀松了下来。你们各自回到自己的思绪里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A little later, Alex checks the time and shifts their bag further under the table, leaving your feet more room.
beats.chinese: 又过了一会儿，Alex 看了看时间，把包往桌子下面挪了挪，为你的脚腾出更多空间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still waiting. But the seat is yours. Have a good morning.
beats.chinese: 还在等，不过座位归你了。祝你早晨愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the Bloomsbury cafe, you recognise Alex at the window table. They look up when you approach.
beats.chinese: 在布卢姆斯伯里的咖啡馆，你认出了窗边的 Alex。你走近时，对方抬起头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. I remember you. The stool's free today. No one to save it for.
beats.chinese: 又见面了，我记得你。今天凳子空着，不用给谁留座。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alex moves their bag beneath their own stool and settles back by the window.
beats.chinese: Alex把包挪到自己的凳子下面，重新靠窗坐好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can stay if you like. I'm happy just sitting here.
beats.chinese: 你愿意的话可以坐。我就这样待着也挺好。

reviewEvidence: 七节点四路径保留并复核；桌面中文空间参照已纠正。全量逐人模型复核、城市横向审校与人工裁决见本版editorial-review-20261114.json；正式发布审校仍待完成。
当前GPT会话逐篇审校记录 editorial-account-review-20261114.json，记录绑定审查、四路阅读、重逢与本轮修订正文指纹。

causality.presenceReason: 熬夜完成博物馆灯光返工后，与朋友约在店里归还借出的望远镜。朋友迟到，因此留下等候。
causality.placeAttitude: 此刻是方便会合和暂歇的中性场所，没有把慢热的灯光技师改成咖啡爱好者或热衷搭讪的人。
causality.stayingConstraint: 朋友明确还需二十分钟。Alex 不离店、不带用户参观博物馆，所有分支留在窗边小桌。
causality.currentGoal: 取回望远镜并度过等候时间，避免因为疲倦强撑交谈。
causality.currentState: 长期对细节耐心、对人慢热。当天夜班后疲倦。主动开口仅因将留给朋友的座位腾给眼前找座位的人。
causality.contactTrigger: 用户在窗边找座位，朋友发来迟到消息，Alex 取走椅上的包，解释这张椅子可以坐。
causality.characterContinuity: 保留博物馆灯光技师职业、观察反光与阴影的兴趣、望远镜、承认自己工作错误的诚实，以及需要具体理由才开口的慢热边界。没有修改性格、价值观、爱好或 personaVoice。
causality.reactionAndChange: 询问长夜才简短谈及返工，并主动结束工作话题。选择安静则先沉默，杯柄阴影触发的是自言自语式说明。继续追问、转开工作、共同注意、继续安静分别有不同回应，不用加好友奖励判定结局优劣。
causality.spatialContinuity: 以同店窗边桌椅实拍为依据，包从旁椅移到桌下，杯子始终位于桌面。没有进入柜台操作区，也没有突然换到室外。
causality.reunionCommonFacts: 已有相遇记录确认用户此前见过Alex Rowan。本次重逢位于布卢姆茨伯里咖啡馆，地点属于当前情境。其余信息由本次可见状态和稳定人物设定提供，适用于新版四条初遇路径与旧活动联系人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the Bloomsbury café, Declan Maher waits at a small window table for a friend to collect him for lunch. His coat is folded on his lap, and the spare chair is empty. He reads a message on his phone, then looks towards you nearby.
beats.chinese: 在布卢姆茨伯里咖啡馆，德克兰·马赫坐在窗边小桌旁，等朋友来找他一起吃午饭。他的外套叠在膝上，旁边的椅子空着。他读了一条手机消息，随后看向附近的你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend says 'the usual'. Is he asking me, or has he already decided for me?
beats.chinese: 朋友说“还是老样子”。这是在问我，还是已经替我决定了？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He keeps the message open on his phone. His coat stays on his lap, and the chair beside him remains empty.
beats.chinese: 他没有关掉手机上的消息。外套仍放在膝上，旁边的椅子一直空着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I used to love that sandwich. Don't fancy it today. I'm Declan, by the way.
beats.chinese: 我以前确实很爱那种三明治。今天却不想吃。对了，我叫德克兰。

choices.english: Mind if I sit for a moment?
choices.chinese: 介意我坐一会儿吗？

choices.english: I'll stay standing. Meeting someone you know from around here?
choices.chinese: 我站着就好。你等的是在这附近认识的朋友吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Declan nods, and you take the empty chair. He looks back at his friend's message with a small, resigned smile.
beats.chinese: 德克兰点点头，你在空椅子上坐下。他又看向朋友的消息，露出一点无奈的笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mate from Dublin. He's getting me the sandwich I ate every day for six weeks.
beats.chinese: 是我在都柏林的朋友。他要给我买那种我连续吃了六个星期的三明治。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He types a short reply, then leaves his thumb hovering over the screen.
beats.chinese: 他打了一句简短的回复，拇指却停在屏幕上方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Can't face another one. I've typed 'lovely'. Very efficient, making my own problems.
beats.chinese: 我现在一个都吃不下了。可我打的是“挺好”。给自己找麻烦，效率倒挺高。

choices.english: You haven't sent it yet. You could just say no sandwich.
choices.chinese: 还没发呢。直接说不用买三明治也行。

choices.english: I'll leave you to your lunch plans. Take care. I get up.
choices.chinese: 那你慢慢安排午饭吧。回见。我站起身。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You remain beside the table. Declan settles the folded coat more securely on his knees.
beats.chinese: 你仍站在桌旁。德克兰把叠好的外套往膝上放稳了些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dublin, actually. We used to play five-a-side. He's over for a visit.
beats.chinese: 其实是在都柏林认识的。我们以前一起踢五人制足球。他过来玩几天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His phone vibrates again. He reads his friend's follow-up message and gives a short laugh.
beats.chinese: 手机又振动了一下。他读完朋友接着发来的消息，短促地笑了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He wants me to choose lunch. I test juice at a plant here. Somehow that makes me responsible for sandwiches.
beats.chinese: 他让我选午饭。我在这边一家果汁厂做感官测试。不知怎么，连三明治也归我负责了。

choices.english: Then what would you recommend for lunch?
choices.chinese: 那你会推荐什么午饭？

choices.english: I'll let you sort that out. Have a good lunch. I step away.
choices.chinese: 那你慢慢决定吧。午饭吃得开心。我走开。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Declan looks at the unsent reply, then deletes it.
beats.chinese: 德克兰看了看那条尚未发送的回复，把它删掉了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair point. 'No sandwich for me, thanks.' Look at that. Fits on one line.
beats.chinese: 也是。“不用给我买三明治了，谢谢。”你看，一行就说完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sends the new message and puts the phone away. His hands return to the coat on his lap.
beats.chinese: 他发出新消息，收起手机，双手重新搭在膝上的外套上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. I'll let you enjoy your seat. I'm going to sit here without arranging any more meals.
beats.chinese: 好了，你安心坐吧。我就在这儿待着，不再安排任何一顿饭了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: As you get up, Declan presses send on the original reply.
beats.chinese: 你起身时，德克兰把原来那条回复发了出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'Lovely' is out in the world now.
beats.chinese: 好了。“挺好”已经发出去了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the phone in his pocket and keeps his coat on his lap, leaving the chair empty.
beats.chinese: 他把手机放进口袋，外套仍留在膝上，没有再占那把空椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll be very pleased to see him, anyway. Take care.
beats.chinese: 反正见到他，我还是挺高兴的。回见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Declan gives an apologetic shrug, without reaching for a menu or naming a place.
beats.chinese: 德克兰略带歉意地耸耸肩，没有找菜单，也没报出任何店名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't give lunch recommendations. I can score a juice sample fairly. Yesterday's favourite sandwich can annoy me today.
beats.chinese: 午饭我就不推荐了。果汁样品我能客观评分，昨天最爱的三明治，今天可能看着就烦。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He types a reply to his friend and sets the phone face down on his own side of the table.
beats.chinese: 他给朋友回了消息，把手机扣放在自己这一侧的桌面上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've told him to choose his own. Safer for everyone. Have a good afternoon.
beats.chinese: 我让他自己选了。这样大家都稳妥。祝你下午愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You step away from the table. Declan raises a hand in farewell.
beats.chinese: 你从桌旁走开。德克兰抬手道别。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers. We'll manage to eat something eventually.
beats.chinese: 谢了。我们总归能吃上点什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He checks the time on his phone, then turns towards the window to watch for his friend.
beats.chinese: 他看了一眼手机上的时间，随后转向窗外，留意朋友有没有到。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He's usually easier to spot than to organise. Take care.
beats.chinese: 一般来说，找到他可比跟他定计划容易。回见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the Bloomsbury café, you see Declan at a window table with a cup and his phone. He recognises you and lifts his hand.
beats.chinese: 在布卢姆茨伯里咖啡馆，你看见德克兰坐在窗边小桌旁，面前放着杯子和手机。他认出了你，抬手招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hello again. I've just checked the football score. Could have spared myself that.
beats.chinese: 哦，又见面了。我刚看了眼足球比分。真是没必要给自己添这个堵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He locks the phone, slips it into his pocket and picks up his cup.
beats.chinese: 他锁上手机，塞进口袋，端起杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three-nil down. Even our Sunday team usually takes longer to manage that. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 零比三落后。就连我们周日那支球队，通常也得多花点时间才能踢成这样。很高兴见到你。

causality.presenceReason: 德克兰提前到布卢姆茨伯里咖啡馆，等一位从都柏林来访、以前一起踢球的朋友来找他一起吃午饭。
causality.placeAttitude: 把窗边小桌当作普通候人地点，心情松弛，愿意与附近的人短聊。旁椅一直空着，但他不以座位使用说明或邀请入座建立接触。
causality.stayingConstraint: 已约好朋友到这里找他，暂时留在窗边桌旁等候。
causality.currentGoal: 等朋友碰面，并处理朋友发来的午饭安排。他还没有决定是迁就朋友，还是明确拒绝自己已经不想吃的三明治。
causality.currentState: 能随口开玩笑，对曾连续吃了六周的三明治却已失去胃口。他知道自己现在不想吃，回复时仍可能下意识迁就朋友。
causality.contactTrigger: 朋友的午饭消息在开场已经到达。德克兰看完手机，主动向附近的玩家问一个有限的措辞问题，朋友说“还是老样子”，究竟是在询问，还是已经替他决定。随后说明自己以前确实很爱那种三明治，今天却不想吃。他没有要求玩家替他决定午饭，也没有转动椅子或用邀请入座作为接触理由。
causality.characterContinuity: 保留德罗赫达成长、都柏林工作经历及因伦敦果汁厂同职能岗位迁居的背景。保留感官测试助理的职业、客观工作判断与反复私人口味的分离、干脆自嘲的语气，以及不把工作能力当作点餐推荐资格的边界。愿意聊天不代表他已经愿意拒绝朋友，礼貌也没有消除他迁就别人的缺点。
causality.reactionAndChange: 玩家可先询问是否能坐一会儿，德克兰点头后玩家坐下，也可选择站着并询问朋友的来历。坐下路径中，他写好迁就的“挺好”却尚未发送。aa中他接受提醒，删掉原回复，明确不要三明治，收起手机结束交谈。ab中他仍发送“挺好”，玩家起身告别，午饭上的迁就保留。站立路径中，朋友又发来让他选择午饭的消息，带出其职业与推荐边界。ba中他婉拒推荐，回复朋友自行选择后结束交谈。bb中玩家直接离开，他挥手道别，转向窗外等人。
